subject: Procurement readiness & pricing packaging alignment - Acme Platform
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Hastings <tom.hastings@acmeplatform.com>, Priya Singh <priya.s@acmeplatform.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: deployment options, procurement path, next steps

Hi Tom / Priya -

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we engage procurement:

Summary of needs we heard on the call:
- Production inference for multi-tenant analytics workloads (peak ~60 concurrent requests, median seq len ~1024).
- Data isolation and audit logs required for regulated workflows (SOC 2 + SSO).
- Preference to pilot quickly, then evaluate reserved capacity for predictable throughput.

Commercial / procurement signals:
- Pilot: small-scale test to validate latency and cost (likely card payment).
- Enterprise: procurement prefers PO for annual commitments.
- Interested in marketplace options (AWS Marketplace) to simplify procurement if we can list.

What we need from you to get procurement moving:
1) Procurement contact (name + email) who will own the PO and contract review.
2) Any internal constraints on fiscal terms / PO process / required SLAs (we heard audit log retention window may be required).
3) Target date for purchase approval (ballpark).

Proposed commercial path (high level):
- Phase 1 (Pilot): Hosted API on on-demand pricing, card payment - low friction & quick onboarding.
- Phase 2 (Enterprise): Move to Dedicated capacity with an annual commit (reserved GPUs) billed via PO to get unit cost savings and isolation.
- Optional: Private deployment or VPC if your security team requires customer-managed network (longer lead time / separate contract).

I've attached a draft SOW and a two-column pricing table that compares hosted(on-demand) vs dedicated(reserved) to illustrate unit economics and commit tiers.

Attachments:
- Redwood_SOW_draft_v1.pdf (SOW stub)
- pricing_table_hosted_vs_dedicated.xlsx (pricing comparison)

Next steps:
- Can you confirm the procurement contact and whether PO vs card is preferred for the pilot?
- If Acme is open to marketplace procurement, we can prioritize listing and provide the marketplace pricing variant in the SOW.

Happy to jump on a short follow-up with procurement if helpful.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (555) 231-9820
[Attachment: Redwood_SOW_draft_v1.pdf (PDF, 160KB)]
[Attachment: pricing_table_hosted_vs_dedicated.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)]

From: Tom Hastings <tom.hastings@acmeplatform.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@acmeplatform.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment options, procurement path, next steps

Thanks Marissa - good summary. A few clarifications from procurement/tech:

Procurement/process notes:
- For pilots we typically use a corporate card or centralized charge; for anything that turns into production we need a PO and an annual commitment.
- Procurement contact is me (Tom Hastings) and I will loop in our legal team if needed.
- Approvals usually take ~2-3 weeks once we have the SOW and pricing.

Technical/security notes (Priya):
- SOC 2 Type II is a must; SSO (SAML) required. Retention windows for audit logs: 12 months minimum.
- Marketplace listing would be ideal to streamline procurement - we can evaluate that alongside the SOW.

We reviewed the SOW and pricing table at a high level; a few asks:
- Can you provide an option for an initial 3-month pilot with on-demand hosted pricing and a conversion path to a 12-month reserved commitment?
- Show a clear delta between hosted on-demand and dedicated reserved (cost per token / cost per hour).

I'll coordinate with our finance team on the PO path. If you can send a DocuSign-ready SOW and updated pricing, I can route it internally.

—Tom
Tom Hastings
Head of Procurement | Acme Platform
tom.hastings@acmeplatform.com | +1 (415) 555-0112

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-09T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: pricing packaging alignment for Acme (pilot -> commit path)

Marissa / Lauren - quick internal note to align pricing and packaging before we send updated materials to Tom:

Recommendation (concise):
1) Pilot Offer (External-facing):
   - Hosted API, on-demand billing, card accepted.
   - 3-month term recommended for quick validation.
   - Include pre-approved upgrade path: 30-day notice to convert to reserved commit.

2) Enterprise Offer (External-facing):
   - Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly or annual commit).
   - Billing via PO for annual commit; include discount tiers: 10% @ 6mo commit, 18% @ 12mo commit, 25%+ for multi-year/large GPU commitments.
   - Optional add-on: Private (VPC/on-prem) - price as an uplift + integration fee.

3) Marketplace / Procurement-friendly variant:
   - Provide an AWS Marketplace SKU with unit pricing that maps to our reserved tiers (slightly higher due to marketplace fees).

Action items for outbound materials:
- Marissa: update pricing_table_hosted_vs_dedicated.xlsx to include a 3mo pilot row, explicit conversion clause, and marketplace SKU column.
- Lauren: validate legal clause for PO billing and approval lead times; confirm SLA language for dedicated offering.
- Aditya: prepare suggested discount tiers and example commit math to convey savings versus on-demand.

We should keep the outbound SOW simple: Pilot (hosted, on-demand) -> conversion language -> Reserved pricing table + marketplace option. Tom asked for DocuSign-ready SOW - let's deliver that.

Thanks,
Aditya
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Hastings <tom.hastings@acmeplatform.com>, Priya Singh <priya.s@acmeplatform.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-09T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment options, procurement path, next steps

Tom / Priya - appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached is an updated SOW (DocuSign-ready) and a revised pricing table that reflects the three-month pilot + conversion path and a marketplace SKU column. Highlights:

- Pilot: Hosted API, on-demand, card ok. 3-month pilot recommended.
- Conversion: 30-day notice to convert pilot usage to a reserved annual commit. We included example math for a 12-month commit vs on-demand.
- Dedicated: Reserved capacity pricing with discount tiers (6mo/12mo/multi-year shown).
- Private: Listed as an add-on with an integration fee and estimated lead time.
- Marketplace: We included an AWS Marketplace SKU; note that marketplace pricing is slightly higher to cover fees - we call that out explicitly.

Attachments:
- [Updated] Redwood_SOW_draft_v1.pdf - DocuSign-ready SOW (placeholder).
- [Updated] pricing_table_hosted_vs_dedicated.xlsx - includes pilot row, conversion clause, marketplace column.

Proposed next steps:
1) Tom: confirm procurement contact & whether finance wants us to deliver via DocuSign or via your marketplace procurement flow.
2) If DocuSign, we'll send the envelope today. If marketplace, we'll start the listing process and share the seller listing docs.
3) We can also kick off a short technical onboarding to validate SOC2/SSO integration during the pilot.

If there are internal legal asks, loop them in and we'll coordinate redlines. Happy to hop on a 20-min procurement/finance call tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (555) 231-9820

Date: 2026-09-10T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment options, procurement path, next steps

Thanks Marissa - documents look good. A few quick confirmations:
- Procurement: we'll route via PO for enterprise commit. For the initial 3-month pilot we'll use centralized card billing.
- DocuSign: please send the envelope to tom.hastings@acmeplatform.com. I'll route it to finance/legal for a ~10 business day review.
- Marketplace: Acme is interested in AWS Marketplace. Please send the seller listing checklist and estimated timeline; if listing takes too long we will go DocuSign/PO.

Next steps on our side: I'll introduce our finance lead (cc'ing shortly) and confirm the internal approval window. Targeting to have a signed PO within 3 weeks of receiving the DocuSign SOW.

Appreciate the quick follow-up.

—Tom
Tom Hastings
Head of Procurement | Acme Platform
